title: Lock the front door: rulesets and the review rules
bridge: A GitHub ruleset is like the required pr Playwright project on a frontend PR, except GitHub enforces it on the branch itself. A direct push to main is refused, even from an admin. A PR cannot merge until every rule passes.
intro: Today nothing stops a bot with write access from merging into fcp main. This lesson agrees the review rules with Nir and Tal, then turns on the fcp ruleset that enforces them. Every later agent depends on this wall.

sections.h: Start with the ruleset that exists today
p: Run this on your laptop: gh api repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/rulesets/5937570 --jq '{name, enforcement}'. It prints main-branch-protection with enforcement disabled. fcp already has a ruleset: a named set of rules that GitHub applies to a branch. Somebody wrote it (1 approval, squash merges) and then switched it off.

So today a bot with write access can push straight to main, and a PR can merge with no review. Our agents will have write access through the GitHub App (lesson g0-2). Before any agent writes code, this ruleset must be on, and the rules it enforces must be agreed by people.
sections.ifInstead: If instead you see HTTP 404, gh is not logged in to a RhinoHealth account. Run gh auth status, then gh auth login.

p: A rule enforced by a machine must be agreed by people first. Otherwise the first blocked PR turns into a debate. G0-01 is a 30-minute meeting with Nir and Tal, with four rules on the table.

One: every PR needs exactly 1 approval. Two: any engineer may review any area, so BE can review FE and the other way round. Three: the requester never approves their own agent's PR. Four: there is no CODEOWNERS file (a GitHub file that assigns reviewers by path), and we do not add one.

Write the agreed rules as one short page in fcp docs/, or in rnd-kb once G6 sets the page format. Announce it in #engineering. Then hand the settings to DevOps for the ruleset (G0-02) and to Platform for the check (G0-09, lesson g0-3).

callout.text: Why one approval and not two? Two approvals double the wait on every PR. The independent-approval check (lesson g0-3) already guarantees that the one approval comes from the right person.

sections.h: Break-glass and who the requester is
p: Two more things get agreed in that meeting. First, the break-glass case: Tal and Nir may merge an urgent production fix without the approval or the checks. GitHub logs every bypass, and Sean reads that list in the weekly review. A bypass that is logged and read is a door in the wall, not a hole.

Second, who the requester of an agent PR is. For Nova it is the person who assigned the Jira ticket to Nova. For a routine (Nova with a different trigger) it is the routine's owner. The requester cannot approve the PR, and neither can anyone who pushed a commit to it.
Lesson g0-3 builds the check that enforces the requester rule. This lesson only writes the rule down, so that the check has something agreed to enforce.

callout.text: The requester never approves their own agent's PR. Every PR needs exactly one approval. Agents never merge, and agents never change rulesets.

p: A required check is a status the PR must show as passed before it can merge. GitHub matches it by the job's name. Today the cloud, client and frontend CI jobs are all named Unit Tests. A required check named Unit Tests would match the wrong job.
Worse, cloud-ci.yml, client-ci.yml and frontend-ci.yaml have paths: filters. A workflow filtered out by paths never starts, so its check stays pending forever, and the PR can never merge.

The fix is two edits per workflow. Rename the jobs to Cloud Unit Tests, Client Unit Tests and Frontend Unit Tests, and remove the paths: filters. The existing check-changes job (the pattern from lesson p2-1) still skips the real work when nothing changed. GitHub counts a skipped job as passed.

callout.text: A paths: filter and a required check do not mix. The filtered workflow never reports, and never reports means never merges.

sections.h: The ruleset call, part 1: who and where
p: The sketch is one bash script that an org admin runs once. It reads the id of a GitHub team, then sends the whole ruleset as JSON to the GitHub API with gh api. The JSON sits in a heredoc: the text between <<EOF and EOF is fed to the command as its input.
We create the team fcp-break-glass first, with Tal and Nir in it. Rulesets cannot name single users as bypass actors (the people or apps allowed to skip the rules), only teams, roles and apps.
sections.because: We replace the disabled ruleset in place with one PUT call, because id 5937570 already exists and keeps its history.

code.file: run once by an org admin: gh api repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/rulesets/5937570 (part 1 of 2)
code.text:
# Run by an org admin. Agents never change rulesets.
# 5937570 is the existing, disabled "main-branch-protection" ruleset on fcp.
TEAM_ID=$(gh api orgs/RhinoHealth/teams/fcp-break-glass --jq .id)   # Tal and Nir

gh api -X PUT repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/rulesets/5937570 --input - <<EOF
{
  "name": "main-branch-protection",
  "target": "branch",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["refs/heads/main"], "exclude": [] } },
  "bypass_actors": [
    { "actor_type": "Team", "actor_id": ${TEAM_ID}, "bypass_mode": "pull_request" }
  ],
  "rules": [
    { "type": "deletion" },
    { "type": "non_fast_forward" },

notes.text: A person with org admin rights runs this. No agent ever gets a token that can change rulesets.
Reads the numeric id of the team fcp-break-glass. The team must exist before this script runs.
PUT replaces the ruleset with this id. --input - means: read the JSON body from standard input, which is the heredoc below.
active turns the ruleset on. Today it says disabled. A third value, evaluate, would only log what it would have blocked.
The ruleset applies to one branch, main. Other branches are not touched.
The one bypass actor: the team, by id. bypass_mode pull_request means they may skip the rules when merging a PR, not when pushing directly.
deletion: nobody can delete the main branch.
non_fast_forward: no force push, so history on main is never rewritten.

sections.h: The ruleset call, part 2: the rules
p: The second half holds the two rules agent PRs meet every day: how a PR is reviewed, and which checks must pass. The lines continue the same JSON; the script is one file.
sections.because: We spell out every review setting, because the defaults GitHub picks are not the rules we agreed in G0-01.

code.file: run once by an org admin: gh api repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/rulesets/5937570 (part 2 of 2)

notes.text: pull_request: a change reaches main only through a PR. This is the line that refuses a direct push.
Exactly 1 approval, as agreed in G0-01.
A new push throws away earlier approvals (a stale approval), so the approval always belongs to the latest commit.
The person who pushed the last commit cannot be the approver. This matches the rule that anyone who pushed a commit cannot approve.
No CODEOWNERS review, because there is no CODEOWNERS file.
Squash is the only merge method, as before.
strict false: a PR need not be rebased on the newest main before merging. strict true would re-run every PR after every merge.
The three contexts are the renamed job names, letter for letter. A typo here means a check that never passes.
EOF closes the heredoc; the JSON above it is sent as the request body.

sections.h: Prove it, export it, keep it
p: A wall you have not pushed against is a guess. Open a test PR with no approval: the merge button is grey, and GitHub says 1 approval and the checks are required. Then open an FE-only PR: the cloud and client checks show as skipped, and after 1 approval it merges.

Export the ruleset with gh api repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/rulesets/5937570 > docs/main-ruleset.json and keep the file next to the review-rules page. The JSON is the record of what we agreed. The ruleset in GitHub is the thing that enforces it.
The I&T gate (e2e_tests) and sdk-ci stay optional for now. Each one waits for a per-cloud QA lock, so they are too slow to require on every PR.

callout.text: Agents never change rulesets. Lesson g0-4 adds a check that fails any agent PR touching a workflow file or the ruleset export.

lab.title: Turn on a ruleset in a scratch repo and push against it
youNeed: gh, logged in to your personal GitHub account (gh auth status)
A public scratch repo on your personal account (rulesets are free on public repos)

worked.do: gh repo create ruleset-lab --public --clone && cd ruleset-lab && git commit --allow-empty -m "first" && git push -u origin main
worked.see:
✓ Created repository <you>/ruleset-lab on GitHub
Cloning into 'ruleset-lab'...
 * [new branch]      main -> main

worked.do:
cat > ruleset.json <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "lab-main",
  "target": "branch",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["refs/heads/main"], "exclude": [] } },
  "rules": [
    { "type": "deletion" },
    { "type": "non_fast_forward" },
    { "type": "pull_request", "parameters": {
        "required_approving_review_count": 1,
        "dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push": false,
        "require_last_push_approval": false,
        "require_code_owner_review": false,
        "required_review_thread_resolution": false,
        "allowed_merge_methods": ["squash"] } },
    { "type": "required_status_checks", "parameters": {
        "strict_required_status_checks_policy": false,
        "required_status_checks": [ { "context": "lab-check" } ] } }
  ]
}
EOF
OWNER=$(gh api user --jq .login); gh api -X POST repos/$OWNER/ruleset-lab/rulesets --input ruleset.json --jq '{id, enforcement}'
git commit --allow-empty -m "direct push" && git push origin main
worked.see:
remote: error: GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/main.
remote: - Changes must be made through a pull request.
 ! [remote rejected] main -> main (push declined due to repository rule violations)

worked.do: ID=$(gh api repos/$OWNER/ruleset-lab/rulesets --jq '.[0].id'); gh api repos/$OWNER/ruleset-lab/rulesets/$ID | jq '.rules[].type'

lab.faded: Same repo, same file: set dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push to true in ruleset.json. Update the ruleset in place with gh api -X PUT repos/$OWNER/ruleset-lab/rulesets/$ID --input ruleset.json. The last step is left to you: export with gh api and jq and show the flag is now true.
lab.alone: Write a second ruleset for release branches in the same repo: ref_name include refs/heads/release/*, 1 approval, no deletion, no force push. No required check this time. Create it with POST and push a branch named release/test. Then try a direct commit on it and see the refusal.
lab.done: A direct push to main in your scratch repo is refused with GH013, and jq lists the four rule types.

quiz.q: Why rename the three CI jobs before turning on the ruleset?

options.text: Because GitHub requires job names to be unique across the whole org.
options.why: Job names only need to be unique inside one workflow; the problem is matching, not a GitHub rule.

options.text: Because a required check is matched by job name, and three jobs named Unit Tests are ambiguous.
options.why: The ruleset lists Cloud, Client and Frontend Unit Tests by name; one shared name would match the wrong job.

options.text: So the frontend tests run before the backend tests.
options.why: Names do not set order; the three workflows run in parallel.

quiz.q: A PR has one approval. The author pushes one more commit. What happens under the ruleset?

options.text: The approval stays, and only the checks run again.
options.why: dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push is true, so the old approval is dismissed.

options.text: The approval is dismissed; someone must approve the new commit.
options.why: An approval always belongs to the latest commit, which is also what the independent-approval check expects.

options.text: GitHub closes the PR and asks for a new one.
options.why: Pushing to a PR branch never closes the PR.

quiz.q: Who may merge an urgent fix into fcp main without an approval?

options.text: Any org admin, because admins are exempt from rulesets.
options.why: Admins are not exempt; only the listed bypass actors are, and the list has one team.

options.text: The rhino-ai-agents App, because it is in bypass_actors.
options.why: The App is never a bypass actor; agents never merge.

options.text: Tal or Nir, through the team fcp-break-glass, and GitHub logs it.
options.why: The team is the only bypass actor, bypass_mode pull_request, and Sean reads the bypass list weekly.

words.plain: A named set of rules GitHub applies to a branch, such as main, before a push or merge is accepted.
A status, matched by job name, that a PR must show as passed before it can merge.
A team, role or app that a ruleset lets skip its rules; every bypass is logged.
The agreed emergency case: Tal or Nir merge an urgent production fix without the rules, and the bypass is read weekly.
The person who asked an agent for a change: whoever assigned the ticket to Nova, or the routine's owner.
An approval given on an older commit; the ruleset dismisses it when a new commit is pushed.
A rule enforced by infrastructure, not by asking nicely; the ruleset is the first wall.

Agree the break-glass case: Tal and Nir can merge an urgent production fix without the approval or the checks. GitHub logs it; Sean reads the list weekly.

Write the rules as one short page in fcp docs/ (or rnd-kb once G6 sets the page format). Announce it in #engineering.
Hand the agreed settings to DevOps for the ruleset (G0-02) and to Platform for the check (G0-09).

tickets.why: This lesson explains every line of the ruleset PUT and why the CI jobs must be renamed first.
walk: In cloud-ci.yml, client-ci.yml and frontend-ci.yaml rename the jobs to Cloud Unit Tests, Client Unit Tests and Frontend Unit Tests. Remove the paths: filters.
Create the GitHub team fcp-break-glass with Tal and Nir, because rulesets cannot name single users as bypass actors.
As an org admin, run the PUT from the sketch against repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/rulesets/5937570.
Export the ruleset with gh api to JSON and keep it with the review-rules page.

Leave the I&T gate (e2e_tests) and sdk-ci optional: the per-cloud QA locks make them too slow to require.

remember: Agree the rules with people first; the ruleset enforces them: one approval, never the requester, no direct push, no agent merge.
